scope: 17 additional traditional-practice source checks on postpartum confinement, culturally safe maternity care and midwifery; study-family linkage and selected funding verification.

checks.findings: English-language systematic review of confinement practices and postpartum depression in Chinese cultures. Language restriction, historical search cutoff and observational confounding limit inference; full included-study membership and disclosures not reviewed.

checks.findings: 2023 systematic review (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0293667): 15 cross-sectional studies and one randomized study; four suggested lower depression risk, two the opposite and ten no significant association. No established protective effect of the whole confinement practice. Publisher reports no specific funding and no competing interests; primary-study funding/overlap and full quality assessment pending.

checks.findings: Systematic review of postpartum rituals and mood/depression using qualitative and quantitative studies. Social support and individual practices cannot be attributed to the entire ritual package; potential overlap with TH2-027/028. Funding and full methods pending.

checks.findings: Malaysian nationwide observational survey of postnatal massage use; associations with parity, income, ethnicity, locality, place of confinement and mode of delivery. checks.findings: Randomized health education program among Chinese women practicing postpartum confinement: 124 recruited, 108 completed (54 in each group). Publisher abstract confirms intervention; direct PubMed body unavailable. OpenAlex indicates Ministry of Education of China, not verified against original funding declaration.

checks.findings: Narrative companion to Guerrero randomized intervention (TH2-080/087): accounts from 26 traditional midwives, 28 apprentices, 12 intercultural brokers and 20 women. Describes implementation and perceived effects, not a second randomized estimate. Authors declare no potential conflicts; article-specific funding pending.

checks.findings: Guerrero pragmatic cluster randomized noninferiority trial in 80 communities across four municipalities; 872 completed pregnancies. Composite perinatal death/childbirth/neonatal complications RD -0.06 (95% CI -0.09 to -0.02); traditional childbirth RD +0.10 (0.02 to 0.18). Retrospective registration ISRCTN12397283, fixed population and mortality uncertainty; not home-birth equivalence or evidence for isolated techniques. Mexican National Council of Science and Technology grant PDCPN-2013-214858; pilot UBS Optimus Foundation; fieldwork Quebec Population Health Research Network and McGill medicine faculty; analysis CeiBA Foundation, Colombian Center of Intercultural Medical Studies and FRQS 255253. Authors declare independence from funders and no competing interests. Full risk-of-bias appraisal pending.

checks.findings: Descriptive Guatemala birthing-center implementation report: 4,322 births through 2023, no maternal deaths at centers and four deaths after referral. No causal comparison with home or hospital births; referral outcomes must remain included. Authors include program implementers (Curamericas) and an Optum affiliation; affiliations alone are not proof of financial conflicts. Funding and full disclosure pending.
